cases.name: Nellie Ann Hicks
cases.about: She was fourth-grade teacher at Ashland School in San Lorenzo, CA who was remembered as a well-liked, respected teacher. She left an abusive husband a decade prior. (Her son David) Hicks called his mother a “hero” who “raised a family of six and she worked full time as as teacher.
cases.caseStatus: COLD CASE SOLVED; FORENSIC INVESTIGATIVE GENETIC GENEALOGY SOLVED; SUSPECT DECEASED WHEN ID'D
cases.narrative: On 5/10/1972, her partially nude body was found by family members who woke up in the morning to discover she had been raped and bludgeoned with a brick wrapped in pantyhose, her head split open by the force of the blows. An intruder had quietly entered her home and attacked her as she slept in her living rooms. Evidence at the scene indicated that her killer entered the home through an unlocked sliding glass door and used manicure scissors to cut her dress and bra. Her adult son and his wife as well as her longtime friend all lived in the home, and were asleep as the slaying unfolded. That led police to suspect that the intruder knocked her unconscious before sexually assaulting her. Hicks’ housemate, a fellow teacher, briefly spoke with her around 1 a.m. the morning of the killing, dozing off on a living room sofa. It was the last time she was seen alive. About four hours later, Hicks’ son discovered her lifeless body in the same room. Hicks’ wallet was missing, though it was later found a few blocks away next to a pair of blood-stained panties.
